sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The codebase under consideration is a legacy banking application developed using Visual Basic 6 (VB6). It is structured around a series of forms and data reports, reflecting the era's typical event-driven programming model. The application appears to manage customer profiles and account workflows, with a strong emphasis on reporting and analytics. The presence of ActiveX/COM components suggests that these are integral to the application's runtime behavior, which will be a key consideration in any modernization effort.

sections.heading: Architectural seams
sections.body: The application exhibits several architectural seams that could be leveraged for modernization. The use of VB6 forms and event-driven handlers, such as those found in `Form:Form1` and `Form:frmExpireItemsWithinDate`, provide clear boundaries where new technologies could be integrated. Additionally, the reliance on ActiveX/COM components indicates potential seams for replacing or updating these components to more modern equivalents. The reporting and analytics pipelines also represent a seam where newer data processing technologies could be introduced.

sections.heading: Risk surface
sections.body: Modernizing this application carries several risks, primarily due to its reliance on outdated technologies like VB6 and ActiveX/COM components. The persistence layer, indicated by elements such as `tblCustomers` and `tblTransaction`, suggests a dependency on legacy SQL/data access logic that may not be compatible with modern databases. Additionally, the event-driven nature of the application could complicate efforts to refactor or replace components without disrupting existing workflows.

sections.heading: Modernization implications
sections.body: To modernize this application, a phased approach is recommended. Initially, replacing the ActiveX/COM components with modern equivalents would reduce dependency on legacy technologies. Next, refactoring the VB6 forms and event handlers into a more contemporary framework could improve maintainability and scalability. Finally, updating the data access layer to support modern databases would enhance performance and integration capabilities. Throughout this process, careful attention must be paid to preserving the existing business logic and workflows to ensure a smooth transition.
